title: Amaranthus: modeled ₹375/qtl left, Kayamkulam → Kondotty
summary: January 2022: reported amaranthus prices at Kayamkulam and Kondotty imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 92% of 25 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹375 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 92 same-variety market pairs screened for amaranthus in January 2022; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Kondotty report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2022
scenes.caption: Kayamkulam (Kerala) and Kondotty (Kerala) both reported amaranthus prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 25 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kayamkulam reported a median ₹2,200 per quintal. Kondotty reported a median ₹2,800 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹700/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹700 per quintal, and Kondotty was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 272 km by road
scenes.caption: 272 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~4 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹58/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹371 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹211 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Kondotty report, the rule selects 23 of 25 modeled shipping days. 22 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹375 per quintal (₹217 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Amaranthus route from Kayamkulam to Kondotty was positive on 92% of matched days in January 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹37,500, or ₹21,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to amaranthus
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹58/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Amaranthus route from Kayamkulam to Kondotty was positive on 92% of matched days in January 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹37,500, or ₹21,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

title: Amaranthus: modeled ₹548/qtl left, Palayam → Kayamkulam
summary: November 2022: reported amaranthus prices at Palayam and Kayamkulam imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 92% of 26 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹548 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 68 same-variety market pairs screened for amaranthus in November 2022; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Kayamkulam report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: November 2022
